subject: toucan
pitch: A keel-billed toucan showing off on a short mossy branch. A huge rainbow beak in lime green, sky blue and orange with a cherry-red tip, a glossy black body, a lemon-yellow bib, a ring of lime-green skin around each eye, bright blue feet and a scarlet patch under the tail. A single pink orchid blooms on the branch beside it.
reasoning:
I'm planning the toucan model proportions, around 0.5m including the beak, perched sideways on a short horizontal branch with a small radius so its body faces forward naturally.

Now I'm sketching out the skeleton: hips root, feet resting on the branch top, a body tilted upright, a tail curving back and down, and a spine chain of points connecting tail, body, and neck to keep everything proportioned and clear of the branch and ground.

Still defining the skeleton chains...

I'm attaching a flattened yellow sphere to the chest for the bib, aiming it at a spine joint, then using a paint function based on surface normal to shade the neck and head yellow toward the front and black elsewhere, mimicking the toucan's throat and cheek markings.

I'll skip body paint and instead paint the neck yellow on the front face, letting the separate bib part blend into black below it. Now I'm sizing up the beak geometry, planning a large upper mandible around 0.17 long and 0.06 tall at the base.

Writing beak paint logic...

Still defining beak geometry...

Now eyes: lime green ring disc on head surface near the beak, with a small black pupil sphere placed on top of it for the toucan's distinctive eye marking.

Next I'll work on the folded black glossy wings, sweeping the shape along the back from shoulder down to tail.

Defining the wing outline shape...

Still working out the tail geometry...

Still working out the tail outline coordinates...

Now I'm setting up the tail joint chain with two segments extending back from the hips, and placing a small flattened red ellipsoid part under the rump for the undertail coverts patch.

For the legs, I'm giving them a short blue limb chain (hip-knee-ankle) running from hip joints down to the feet, and planning zygodactyl toes—two forward, two back—to wrap around the branch for perching.

Working out the toe placement on the branch's curved surface, mapping circle points at different angles to get the toes wrapping naturally over the top, with two toes curling forward and two curling back, each a small rounded cylinder off the ankle joint.

Setting up the toe chains and claw spikes, then checking how the hip-to-ankle leg aligns with the body's belly curve to make sure the leg geometry connects properly at the bottom.

Checking the body radius near the hips to make sure the joint sits inside, then sketching the branch as a slightly curved sweep path with a roughly 0.05 radius along its length.

Tweaking the radius taper slightly so the branch ends lift a bit rather than staying perfectly flat, and planning the branch paint as a moss-on-top coat using countershade over a mottled moss/bark base so the top reads green and the underside reads bark brown.

Now adding small flattened moss lumps scattered across the branch top surface where it faces upward, plus a secondary twig sprouting off the main branch end with its own taper, and sketching leaf outlines to extrude onto that twig for foliage.

Now I'm planning the orchid placement beside the branch, with a curving green stem rising to a flower head, where the Phalaenopsis bloom will be built from lateral petals, sepals, and a lip extruded around a center point facing forward.

Defining petal and sepal outlines...

Still designing the leaf shapes...

I'll just assign the bone hips to all the scenery parts for simplicity, since joints like sweeps, extrudes, and scatter all inherit bone attachment the same way. For the head, I'm placing a sphere part at the head joint with slight scaling to shape it, and leaving crown feathers out for now since they're optional detail.

Now I'm checking the head sphere position against the neck end point to make sure they connect properly, then working through the beak geometry — upper and lower loft stations defined by position, width, and height at each point along the beak's length — and I'm noticing the lower jaw's top edge slightly overlaps the upper beak's bottom edge, which I need to adjust.

Adjusting beak overlap values...

That seems close enough, with slight touching between upper and lower bottoms. I'm placing the jaw joint and setting up a catmull loft through the station centers with interpolated heights and widths, using bone attachments for upper and lower parts. For the beak paint I'm using the loft's surface parameter, and adding a small black nostril sphere near the base along with the existing dark base outline.

Now I'm working out the color banding along the beak length: a thin black line near the base around t 0.2-0.26, then blue sides up to about t .45, orange past that, lime on top, and red at the very tip past t .9, sharing the same paint logic between upper and lower mandibles with the tip color swapped to red.

I'm defining the palette now—black, yellow, lime, sky blue, orange, red, scarlet, feet blue, pink—and setting up the body as a radius-varying sweep along the spine chain with rounded caps, then doing the same for the neck with a yellow front patch that should blend into the head's yellow coloring.

For the head paint, I'm trying different normal-based conditions to get a yellow cheek/throat patch against the black that doesn't accidentally swallow the beak area, with the eye ring sitting near the black border above. Then I'm positioning a chest bib ellipsoid near the body's front, checking it lines up with where the spine path ends and the body radius tapers.

Still working out stick placement...

Actually simpler to skip the separate bib geometry entirely and just paint the yellow bib directly onto the body surface using normal and height thresholds, which conforms naturally without clipping issues.

Now I'm setting up the joint hierarchy: head attaches to neck, with named chains for neck, spine, tail, legs, digits, and jaw, each using role labels. I'm mapping out the spine as a 4-point path yielding three segments via catmull interpolation, matching the neck's two-point chain structure.

Working out toe placement now, computing arc positions for each toe joint based on foot anchor coordinates and angle offsets to form a curved digit chain with two segments per toe.

For the zygodactyl foot structure I'm setting up four toes per leg—two facing forward, two backward—looping through direction and offset values to generate eight toe chains total across both legs, then moving on to defining the leg limb chains with their bend directions.

Now I'm adding small anatomical touches: a dark "trousers" ellipsoid near the hip for tufted thigh feathering, sweeping the leg chain with a thin cylindrical profile and blue coloring, and considering whether to include extra details like white tail coverts or additional body feather cards, though I'm deciding to skip those for simplicity. I'm also noting the dark beak tip detail before moving forward.

For finer features, I'm skipping serrated beak edges but adding nostril dots as tiny black spheres embedded into the upper beak surface, locating them by finding the nearest surface point near the beak's side rather than guessing exact coordinates. I'm reasoning through how the loft geometry's width tapers so the nearest-surface lookup will land correctly, and similarly handling the eye placement by finding points relative to the head part's surface. Finally, I'm scattering small flattened spheres across the branch surface to represent moss lumps, using a filtered random distribution that favors upward-facing areas with minimum spacing between clumps.

Now I'm working out moss coloring by alternating between two green shades and refining the scatter filter to avoid placing moss near the bird's feet by excluding points too close to the center x-axis. I'm also planning the orchid flower's color palette—pink sepals and petals, a darker magenta lip, yellow column with spots, and a tiny yellow center sphere—along with buds positioned along a curved stem built from a few control points, including a short branching stem leading to two differently-sized bud spheres. I'm starting to define the petal-generating function that will build each flower shape from an outline, angle, color, and depth offset relative to the flower's center point.

Still writing petal placement logic...

I'm also deciding to keep the design modest by adding a small twig stub with just a few leaves rather than a fuller branch, and considering whether the wing should have a slightly blue-black tint instead of plain black.

I'm checking that the branch and legs rest properly at floor level by tuning the catmull-rom path and radius arrays so the bottom sits near zero without dipping below it, and confirming everything attaches rigidly to the hips bone for the sweeps. Now I'm starting to write the helper code for ball geometry parts.

Still writing eye details... adding sphere, pupil, and highlight geometry with embed offsets, plus guarding against null hit results before moving on to define the paint functions for coloring the beak.

Writing paint function logic...
